answer: An agent market requires each seller identity to lock a bond for 30 days before bidding on jobs, whether sourcing opal, reserving harbor berths, or finding ivory substitutes. The bond stays locked until all accepted jobs clear a dispute window, and proven non-delivery forfeits it. Creating accounts is cheap, but activating a thousand sellers requires a thousand bonds, tying up the attacker's capital and putting it at risk on every fraudulent sale.
